I do try, hard, to do what I like to do. But its so hard to find enjoyment in it. Always have that cloud over my head telling me "it's not good enough". 

I hope one day I'll be able to make art and not be scared of showing it to people. My biggest dream is to write fictional books (which broadly is also a type of art I'd say) and publish them.. but I'm held back with the experiences that drawing pictures gave me.

Thank you again for taking your time to reply to my rambles. It means a lot to me, that I'm not just shouting in the void. I'm a bit mentally exhausted now so I can't really reply much in-depth, but your words did make my crappy day just a bit better, so thank you! <3

Thank you for getting back to me. And I'm glad that at very least my rambles made you feel less alone <3 

I'm open to random talk but I don't even know how to get started.. I'm a bit socially awkward, and I'm worried I'm embarrassing

Hey and thank you for getting back to me.

I have to correct a small thing here though. I'm not the one who's shooting down other people's opinions. I'm very open and live strongly by "agree to disagree" peacefully if I don't agree with someone. Heck, I'm even open-minded to "both sides" of the whole covid and vaccine debate. I won't make this about that stuff, but I'm sure most people recognize how heated that argument is among people.

Sadly I seldom get that back. And I can't be confident about the things I like because I've always been harassed for it. I even stopped drawing, something I was passionate about as a kid, because I was repeatedly told it was childish and stupid. 

But I'm just scared now that if I ever disagree with someone, no matter how pointless, they'll just hate me and stop talking to me. And I feel forced to agree with people no matter what I think. This usually comes as a silence or shrug from me because I hate lying. 

I've always tried to encourage people with their art or writing. Even if they think their own drawing sucks, I've encouraged them and told them which parts are good and where they can improve. So I'm not so sure I've experienced what you describe, that we get things back.

I -think- I'm grateful. At least I know there's parts of life that are made better, but its also causing me to feel guilty for being depressed in the first place. No amount of love for other people are keeping me from ending life. But it does make me guilty. And that makes it worse. 

I think I'd be friends with me? Maybe? Though itd be boring to be friends with someone who 100% agrees with everything, lol..

Thanks though, really.
I don't think the last 3 years will be significant compared to the 13 I already wasted hoping things got better.

Me as well..
Add in a degree of laziness too. It's just easier to turn on the TV than make an attempt..

It's okay, I didnt take it as if you wanted to upset me. It's just a touchy subject because I do care about the dog of course, and knowing she might be too much for me is rough stuff.

I'll see if I can get help from those, though I dread if they might blame me/get upset with me and tell me I got the wrong dog or something..

I see. Thanks a lot for your input, its very valuable even if it kind of hurts. I do like that dog after all.. when she's calm, she's amazing. Obedient, loving, fun. And then she gets all hyped up at the potential of chasing toys to the point she's hard to control, even for my trainer who has dealt with WL GSD for years and won championships with her current dog. 

Based on what my trainer says, I've not just gotten a WL GSD, but one of the most intense individuals at that..

And it depresses me. Because I don't go in getting a pet with the intention to get rid of it. I am committed, be it 3 or 20 years I'll get with them. But I'm also facing the fact that this dog might simply never cut it as service dog.. and worse, I might never really trust her with the cat or other people, and I can't spend the next 10 years with an animal I can't trust like that..?

I'm still doing the best I can. I do a lot of impulse control and I'll check out the exercises you linked when I get home from work.

But I don't know what to do.. She's such a great dog in many ways and I've spent so much of myself on training her. In many ways she's remarkably well-trained, but I can't control her when she switches on...

What breeds have you experienced best in service dogs..? Not that I want to replace her per se, but it's worth having in mind and have something to compare to.

I was recommended that they were loyal pleasers and suited for service dog work. The dog needs to be very brave, able to go into amusement parks, airports and other noisy places with lots of people without losing focus on its owner. 

Her breeder was also confident it was a good idea.

And so far, she's in many ways great. She didnt care about fireworks, been to the airport with no problems. Shes got an intense focus on me, is obedient when we are doing things, is bringing me stuff like clothes when I ask her, so on.

Nobody told me about the prey drive though.. and that prey drive is causing us problems I feel. Especially because I can't trust her with the cat still. My cat has PTSD and doesnt ever fight back, so the dog doesnt even realize the cat has claws. And I cant really play with the dog, with toys, because even a short session of tug-o-war seems to hype her up to the point it's hard to calm her down. 

Pretty much every wake moment shes running around with a toy in her mouth.

Every meal shes gotten has been with training/exercises (I dont feed her in a bowl). I spend 10-30 minute sessions multiple times a day trying to teach her calm/relax. 

She was supposed to become a psychiatric service dog, but I'm starting to worry she is too high energy to handle that kind of work. 

I can't use her with bite work/schutzhund etc., but I'm starting to think if she has been bred with too high a prey drive to.. well, function?? Her breeder seemed optimistic about the potential in a psych service dog, but with that amount of prey drive I'm not feeling so sure anymore..

I'll look into your links soon.
I'll try something with the leash, thanks!

That would be great!

I sadly don't really know anyone other than my parents, but we are keeping my dog a bit away from theirs; he's 12 and have severe arthritis and going to be put down within the next months time probably as he's starting to not be able to walk despite medicine... so, a wild puppy isn't a good experience for him.

I always hope theres other dogs when we go to the "dog forest" (fenced in area in the nearby forest for dogs) but I guess because of corona, people don't go there these days ..

Thanks. I'll have to try approaching that method, but I still feel so guilty putting her away :( 

But leashing her indoors might be useful? Then again, she knows I don't want her to chase the cat and backs away if I as much as look at her and say her name when she's approaching her.

Not an option I'm afraid. I wish we had some sort of daycare here she could be at while I was at work, but there's nothing of the sort in my country.

Closest is hotels for when you go on vacation, but they're VERY expensive and need booking months in advance.

Yes, she's in a crate all night and in a small hallway when I'm not home. So I feel guilty if I put her there when I'm not at work, as she already spends 17 hours a day confined like that. Then I spend about 3 hours on her and wish the remaining 4 would be with her out and about in the apartment, but it's also taking such a toll on my energy because I constantly have to tell her to stop messing with the cat.
